page: Vultr vcg-a16-6c-64g-16vram is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Dedicated Metal GPU family. It features an Intel processor with 6 vCPUs mapped to 3 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a 350 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. Although categorized under the Dedicated Metal GPU family with NVIDIA listed as the GPU manufacturer, the active GPU count is zero.

Benchmark data shows average performance across most standard compute and memory tasks. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is 1745.38, and the multi-core score is 10619.81. Memory bandwidth is measured at 586.08 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 76.25 GB/sec for large-block reads and 43.9 GB/sec for large-block writes. Notably, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing, achieving 8771.1 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and 591.21 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, scoring 30.39 GB/sec.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of over 10 GB per core and the inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage, this server offers a resource-dense profile for memory-bound workloads. It is suitable for database operations, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
